links.outcome: Hallucination rate of medical LLM with knowledge-grounded calibration versus standard federated baselines
links.effect: FedKGC achieved a 28% reduction in hallucination rates compared with standard federated baselines on non-IID MIMIC-IV partition and MedHallu benchmark, under differential privacy.
links.quote: Evaluation on a non-IID partition of the MIMIC-IV dataset and the MedHallu benchmark demonstrates that FedKGC achieves a 28% reduction in hallucination rates compared to standard federated baselines while strictly adhering to $(\epsilon, \delta)$-Differential Privacy guarantees.

unlisted_practices: Federated learning with differentially private metadata and a global conflict map to down-weight contradictory concepts
Knowledge-grounded loss anchoring LoRA fine-tuning to clinical guidelines

screen.reason: The paper develops and benchmarks a novel federated training and retrieval-augmented calibration framework (FedKGC) on benchmark datasets (MIMIC-IV, MedHallu) rather than testing an organizational deployment safeguard.
